steps.title: Prepare A+ trace components
steps.instruction: Add 500 mL deionized water to a 1 L glass bottle and stir continuously while adding 3.43 g H₃BO₃, 0.0315 g ZnCl₂, 0.003 g MoO₃, and 0.0004 g vitamin B12; prepare 100 mL stock solutions of FeCl₃·6H₂O (3.89 g/L), MnCl₂·4H₂O (4.3 g/L), CuSO₄·5H₂O (0.003 g/L) and CoCl₂·6H₂O (0.012 g/L); add 1 mL of each stock to the bottle and bring the volume to 1 L with water; store all stock solutions and the trace‑component solution refrigerated.

steps.title: Prepare A+ medium
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL stock solutions of Na₂EDTA·2H₂O (0.3 g/L), KCl (6 g/L), CaCl₂·2H₂O (3.7 g/L), NaNO₃ (10 g/L), KH₂PO₄ (0.5 g/L) and Trizma base (adjusted to pH 8.2); in a 1 L glass bottle add 500 mL deionized water, 18 g NaCl and 5 g MgSO₄·7H₂O, then add 10 mL of each stock solution while stirring; fill to 1 L, adjust pH to 7.6 with HCl, autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi for 20 min, cool, and filter‑sterilize‑add 10 mL A+ trace components (0.22 µm); store the final medium at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare A+ modified medium
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL stock solutions of MgSO₄·7H₂O (5 g/L), Na₂EDTA·2H₂O (0.3 g/L), KCl (6 g/L), CaCl₂·2H₂O (3.7 g/L), NaNO₃ (10 g/L), KH₂PO₄ (0.5 g/L) and Trizma base (pH 8.2); in a 1 L glass bottle add 500 mL deionized water, then add 10 mL of each stock solution, fill to 1 L, adjust pH to 7.6, and filter‑sterilize‑add 10 mL A+ trace components; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Assemble and sterilize culture flask
steps.instruction: Cut silicone pipes to the desired length, mount them on the olives of 1 L bottle lids, install check valves at the intake and a 0.22 µm sterile filter at the outlet olive, close the bottles, cover pipe ends with aluminum foil, then autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi for 20 min and let cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Inoculate and grow cyanobacteria
steps.instruction: Under sterile conditions add 500 mL A+ medium to the sterilized flask and inoculate with Picosynechococcus sp. PCC 7002; close the flask and incubate at 25 °C with discontinuous full‑spectrum light (~30 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹, 18 h light/6 h dark) and a slight pressurized air supply for mixing until stationary phase (OD₇₅₀ > 4) is reached.

steps.title: Harvest cells for ALS‑gel
steps.instruction: Collect 400 mL of the culture at OD₇₅₀ = 0.3 under sterile conditions, centrifuge at 7,000 × g for 2 min at room temperature, discard the supernatant and keep the cell pellet.

steps.title: Prepare gelatin‑based ALS‑gel
steps.instruction: Fill 400 mL A+ modified medium in a 1 L glass bottle, heat to 45 °C on a magnetic stirrer at 300 rpm, dissolve 40 g gelatin until the solution is transparent yellowish and homogeneous, cool to 40 °C and slowly add 3.36 g NaHCO₃, adjust pH to 7.6 with HCl or NaOH, add 5.73 g CaCl₂·2H₂O while reducing stirring speed to avoid foam, cool to 37 °C, add the cell pellet, and incubate for 10 h at 37 °C under continuous full‑spectrum light (180 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) with moderate stirring (temperature set slightly below 37 °C to avoid overshoot).

steps.title: Mix sand with ALS‑gel
steps.instruction: Brush a thin layer of virgin rapeseed oil onto the steel three‑gang mold, weigh 1.35 kg ISO standard sand into a metal bowl, add 198.50 g prepared ALS‑gel and gently mix with a spatula (prepare the mixture individually for each 1 × 3 prism mold; note ~50 mL gel remains when preparing 2 × 3 prisms).

steps.title: Hand‑mix and fill mold
steps.instruction: At room temperature hand‑mix the sand‑gel mixture until it becomes slightly viscous, mixing once every 5 min after the initial thorough mixing; avoid excessive mixing to prevent air bubbles and foam; press the mixture into the steel mold with a spatula.

steps.title: Cure and demold prisms
steps.instruction: Place the filled mold in a refrigerator at 8 °C for at least 6 h; then detach the mold and transfer the prisms onto metal grates to dry at 20–22 °C, 40–60 % relative humidity, protected from direct sunlight, for at least 14 days until mass equilibrium is reached.

steps.title: Test mechanical strength of prisms
steps.instruction: After drying, mount each prism on a universal testing machine (ZwickRoell) according to DIN EN 196‑1:2016‑11; perform a three‑point bending tensile test at 50 ± 10 N/s (load‑controlled), then a uniaxial compressive failure test at 2,400 ± 200 N/s; test three replicates for each of six cyanobacteria‑containing prisms and six control prisms and record the bending tensile and compressive strengths.
